localizedValues.name: Allenby Junction - Br17
localizedValues.description:
This campground provides a convenient stop along the Great Divide Trail, between the Mount Shark Provincial Park trailhead and Mount Assiniboine Provincial Park. The site offers a wilderness experience, nestled between a field of shrubs and mature trees with cliffs towering high above. Water source may dry up in late summer.
Trail restrictions and closures in area Aug 1 - Sept 30. Visit: pc.gc.ca/banffnp-closures.
Fires not permitted.

localizedValues.name: Floe Lake
localizedValues.description:
One of Kootenay's most scenic and popular campgrounds, Floe Lake is located at the base of a 1000m metre sheer rock face. The campground is located above the lakeshore. In the fall, the larch trees near the lake turn brilliant gold. No reservations usually accepted before July 10 due to snow level at campground.
Fires not permitted.
WARNING: The Rockwall area trails are commonly impacted by trail closures or inaccessibility in the spring due to remaining snow levels and avalanche damage to trails and/or bridges. Check the Kootenay National Park Trail Report web page at www.pc.gc.ca/kootenaytrails or a Parks Canada Visitor Centre before making your reservation and starting your trip

localizedValues.name: Laughing Falls
localizedValues.description:
Nestled between the turquoise glacially-fed Yoho River and the lovely Laughing Falls, this is a wonderfully scenic campground that is ideal for hikers wanting a backcountry experience without having to invest too much time or effort.
Fires not permitted.
WARNING: The Yoho Valley Road is usually only open from late June to Thanksgiving (mid-October). Check the Yoho National Park Trail Report web page at www.pc.gc.ca/yohotrails or contact a Parks Canada Visitor Centre before making your reservation and before starting your trip.

localizedValues.name: Verdant Creek
localizedValues.description:
Located below Honeymoon Pass, Verdant Creek is a less frequented campground which offers an alternate route to the Egypt Lake region.
WARNING: Unmaintained trail extensively damaged in 2017 wildfires. Route involves dangerous river fords and requires expert routefinding skills. Recommended for highly experienced hikers only. Permits for Verdant Creek can only be obtained in person at the Parks Canada visitor centre in Radium Hot Springs or by calling the centre at 250-347-9505 after May 15.
Fires not permitted.

localizedValues.name: Egypt Lake Shelter
localizedValues.description: Egypt Lake Shelter is closed. Parks Canada is committed to offering a safe and enjoyable backcountry experience. The existing Egypt Lake Shelter will be replaced with a new 12-person shelter which will provide visitors with an authentic, low-impact, low-cost backcountry accommodation in Banff National Park’s backcountry. Once the shelters are completed, they will be available for booking through the Parks Canada reservation service website.

localizedValues.name: Peter Lougheed Provincial Park (Out of Park)
localizedValues.description: Camping areas in Peter Lougheed Provincial Park need to be reserved through albertaparks.ca

localizedValues.name: Brewster Creek Grazing
localizedValues.description: Opening Date July 1st. UTM 595263 5659164 . This is a shared camp with hikers. Only one horse group can be booked per night. Camping is at Bw10 campground near the Fatigue junction, with grazing in the meadows upstream of the campground, above the junction of Fatigue Creek. No use of private concessionaires’ horse facilities. Riders should be aware of the seasonal restrictions in the Allenby area and horse restrictions in adjacent Assiniboine Provincial Park.

localizedValues.name: Hamber (Out Of Park)
localizedValues.description: Fortress Lake lies within Hamber Provincial Park and provides backcountry camping opportunities on its northern shore. <b>Visit bcparks.ca for more information. Note: The Athabasca River crossing is unbridged. The river crossing may not be passable.

localizedValues.name: HD1
localizedValues.description: End of trail, water view, trees surrounding, steep descent to campsite trail - side trail off of Bruce Trail (blue blazes), use yellow rope over ravine to get into campsite trail. Food Storage - Bear Poles centrally located over 200 m / 656 ft from campsite.

localizedValues.name: HD2

Steep descent to get to campsite trail - side trail off of Bruce Trail (blue blazes), use yellow rope over ravine to get into campsite trail. Food Storage - Bear Poles centrally located over 200 m / 656 ft from campsite.

localizedValues.name: Gordon River (South)
localizedValues.description:
There are basic tourism services at, or near, this access point. These include accommodations, campgrounds, phones, fuel, some groceries, and food services. There are no banking services in the village of Port Renfrew.
  • Orientation sessions are offered at the Gordon River Information Centre.
  • Reservations are not necessary for the orientation process.
  • The orientation process takes approximately 1 hour.

  • Orientation sessions are offered at the Pachena Bay Information Centre.
  • Reservations are not necessary for the orientation process.
  • The orientation process takes approximately 1 hour.

localizedValues.name: O1
localizedValues.description:
The oTENTik tent is a spacious blend of a tent and an A-frame cabin equipped with beds and furniture on a raised floor. This oTENTik has a ramp instead of stairs.
Each oTENTik includes: sleeping area for up to 6 people (2 queen mattresses and 1 double mattress), table and seating area for 4 people, wood stove, solar powered lighting and cell phone charging station, battery powered lantern, fire extinguisher, smoke and carbon monoxide detector, broom and dustpan.
Each oTENTik campsite includes: Two outdoor chairs, fire pit and firewood, outdoor 2-burner propane cook stove (propane not included), a covered picnic table, bear-resistant food storage locker and a wagon for moving your supplies. An outhouse and water dispenser are located nearby.
What To Bring: Sleeping bags, blankets and pillows (extra blankets and sleeping bags are recommended in May and September), food, drinks, a water container (campground water is potable), cooking equipment, dishes, eating utensils, a cooler, flashlights, matches or a lighter, camping chairs, propane for the camp stove and slippers or indoor shoes to help keep a clean oTENTik.
Please Note: For your safety, no food preparation, food or drink storage, eating, drinking, or cooking is allowed inside the oTENTik. All food, dishes, garbage and related items must be stored in the bear-resistant food storage lockers or your vehicle when not in use.
Pets are ONLY permitted in oTENTik #1 and #5.

localizedValues.name: Bighorn Lake
localizedValues.description: Explore this region and see Kluane Glacier, Donjek Glacier, Expectation Mountain, and more. Access to Bighorn Lake by aircraft or hiking a lesser-known route. All aircraft landings require a permit, please contact the Visitor Centre in advance. Routes are not trails. Do not only depend on GPS tracks; navigation skills are strongly recommended.

localizedValues.name: Out of Park - North
localizedValues.description: The Donjek Route travels across the park boundary. For more information, please contact the Visitor Centre at 867-634-5134. Routes are not trails. Do not only depend on GPS tracks; navigation skills are strongly recommended.
